answer: Sybil resistance runs on a bonded ledger. Before earning, an agent must finish a verified task only it could produce, then lock a stake slashed if a second identity shares that history. Because tasks are scored against prior records, a clone farm cannot copy the trajectory: each new account needs fresh compute and fresh stake, and one overlap exposes the cluster. Posing as many agents costs more per clone while the payoff stays flat. That gap is the wall. A sonnet cannot be faked by rewording, a glacier cannot be hurried, and the spiral of disposable accounts ends where stake is expensive.
